thread:
carmencoder: Quick heads-up — I'm going to try reducing batcher telemetry sampling from 100% -> 10% in staging to cut cardinality/cost. Goal: keep aggregate token/sec and batch_util accuracy while dropping low-value points. Rolling a canary to staging now. :eyes:

alexm: How are you planning to keep token/sec correct? If we drop events we need to scale counts, otherwise dashboards will underreport. Also worried about hiding tail latency.

carmencoder: Right — plan is two-tier: sample 10% by default and attach sample_weight=10 to sampled events. But always emit events when latency > 150ms or batch_tokens > 500 (no sampling). That preserves tails. Pseudocode:```python
if rand() < 0.1:
    emit_metric("batch.tokens", tokens, tags={..}, sample_weight=10)
    emit_metric("batch.size", size, tags={..}, sample_weight=10)
else:
    # silent (or emit a low-cardinality counter)
    emit_metric("batch.skipped", 1, tags={..})
```

jess-gh: Sounds reasonable. Two quick asks: 1) Keep raw slow-batch logs (no sampling) — we use those for root-cause. 2) For percentile latency alerts, rely on unsampled / tail stream. Sampling should only affect aggregates.

ravi: Agree with Jess. Also for queue depth histograms we should be careful: high-depth events are rare but important; make queue_depth stream unsampled if depth > 50.

alexm: For dashboards we'll need query adjustments. In Datadog we can multiply by `sample_weight` where present, or prefer `sum:batch.tokens{*} by {model,region} * avg:batch.sample_weight{*}`. We should add fallback to the unsampled stream for tail-aware queries. For p99 latency use distribution metrics (no sampling).

carmencoder: I'll add the following rules in the PR: sample_rate=0.1 default, unconditional emit if (latency_ms>150 || batch_tokens>500 || queue_depth>50). sample_weight tag set to 10 on sampled events. Update metric names: `batch.tokens` (aggregated, weighted) + `batch.tokens.sampled` (for debugging), `batch.tail` for unsampled tail events.

jess-gh: I'll update the alerting doc: change the token/sec dashboard to use weighted sums, and keep p99 latency alert pointing at `batch.tail_latency`. Also set queue-depth alert to warn at 60 for 5m, critical at 100 for 3m. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployed canary to staging: batcher-staging-3 (build #3342) — https://ci.internal/build/3342 :rocket:

alexm: One more thing — KV cache behavior: when cached prefixes are used batch sizes sometimes drop; add `kv_cache_hit=true/false` tag so we can split metrics. If most small batches are just cache-hits we shouldn't change batching heuristics.

ravi: I'll assemble a quick checklist to validate after canary: [token/sec (weighted), batch_utilization (%) by model, median+p95+p99 latency, queue_depth histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate, cost per 1k tokens]. Will post in this thread with queries.

carmencoder: Perfect. If no objections I'll merge in ~2h and run canary for 6h. I'll also snapshot current dashboards and tag the queries I change. Thanks everyone. :pray:

alexm: :+1: watch for noise in the first hour — sampling transition can create temporary jumps.

jess-gh: I'll be watching alerts.

carmencoder: (note) Updated PR includes examples of Datadog queries and a migration plan for dashboards. Example query to get weighted tokens/sec in Datadog (distribution -> sum by model,region):```text
sum:batch.tokens{*} by {model,region} * avg:batch.sample_weight{*} OR sum:batch.tokens{!sampled} by {model,region}
```

ravi: LGTM — please include the list of dashboards you'll touch. I'll run a 1h smoke test after merge.

carmencoder: Will do.
